description: Targeted review of poorly covered parties, including Arabic-language research. Explicit reviewed replacements retain prior evidence.

AR_HB_SERVICE26.title: Al-Ittihad: Hadash–Balad statement against conscription
AR_HB_SERVICE26.note: Joint statement explicitly attributed to these two parties; not generalized to Ta’al or Ra’am.

AR_TAAL_INQUIRY.title: Radio Nas: Ahmad Tibi on an October 7 inquiry
AR_TAAL_INQUIRY.note: Direct interview; visible page lacks a publication date. Discussion concerns passage of the 2026 budget. Appointment mechanism not specified.

AR_TAAL_POLICE25.title: Knooz: Tibi calls on police to fight criminal organizations
AR_TAAL_POLICE25.note: Individual reactions are attributed separately. Opposition to banning a community organization does not establish a blanket position on Shin Bet assistance.

AR_RAAM_CRIME26.title: Kul al-Arab: Abbas press conference on policing
AR_RAAM_CRIME26.note: Reported party-leader press conference; criticism of the proposed Shin Bet intervention is not treated as opposition to every possible intelligence role.

AR_RAAM_BUDGET26.title: Radio Nas: Abbas opposes cuts to the five-year development plan
AR_RAAM_BUDGET26.note: Interview explicitly discusses 2026, but the visible page does not give a publication date. Protecting budgets does not establish a tax policy.

AR_HADASH_ED26.title: Al-Ittihad: Hadash teachers’ faction education statement
AR_HADASH_ED26.note: Indexed Arabic statement from Hadash’s teachers’ faction. Scope is education; does not establish a nationwide fiscal package.

YNET_TRANSPORT26.title: Ynet: parties’ responses on Shabbat transport
YNET_TRANSPORT26.note: Uses attributed party responses, not voter polling. Joint List response is not silently assigned to individual component parties.

RZ_GAZA26.title: News1: Smotrich advocates Israeli government and settlements in Gaza
RZ_GAZA26.note: Reported speech by the party leader; distinguishes his proposal from adopted government policy.

STATEHOOD26.title: JDN: party leaders respond to Abbas’s statehood statement
STATEHOOD26.note: Positions are assigned only to the named speakers. Eisenkot’s statement concerns the government he proposes to form.

O710.title: Otzma Yehudit: Disengagement 710 programme
O710.note: Reviewed as a current campaign document. Its emigration mechanism does not specify the quiz’s civil-administration model.

M.title: Reservists: platform
M.note: Full live programme reviewed on 2026-09-29, including service, crime, term limits and competition. Undated; not labelled as a new manifesto.

BA.title: Balad: political program
BA.note: Arabic text reread directly. Page bears 2017-03-29 but contains later references as well as older passages; revision dates are unclear. Kept historical, with separately labelled continuity inferences.

limitations: Arabic research was conducted separately for Hadash, Balad, Ta’al and Ra’am. Joint statements are assigned only to their named signatories; coalition membership and voters’ opinions do not establish party policy.

Balad’s official programme carries a 2017 page date but contains material from different periods. It is kept historical. Continuity on constitutional equality, wealth taxation and collective bargaining is an explicit 60%-weighted inference, not a verified 2026 pledge.

Undated interviews remain undated. Hadash’s education statement was available through indexed Arabic text; direct retrieval was intermittent. Sector-specific demands establish only a broad spending direction, not a complete nationwide fiscal package.

Likud’s transport response retains historical exceptions and private operations. The closest existing service value means no general public network; its exceptions are explained in the interface. Yashar’s statehood statement concerns a government it would form, not a permanent final-status framework.

Religious Zionism’s September 2026 judicial proposals mention an override but do not establish the majority threshold in the retrieved text. Older judicial positions remain historical. Otzma’s official campaign page was reviewed but does not settle our long-term Gaza administration component.
The same transport survey contains a newer Democrats response that warrants a separate reconciliation with its earlier programme. This targeted pass did not recode that already better-covered party.

Large gaps remain, especially for Likud, Otzma Yehudit, Ta’al and Religious Zionism. Unknowns still earn zero points and stay in the denominator. Current evidence was not found for every education, labour, climate, marriage or housing component.
